noteGrp.note: A chronicle in twelve books compiled in Syriac from a variety of sources by an anonymous Syriac Orthodox author, possibly a monk living at Amida, in the second half of the 6th century. Books 1–2 include narratives such as the history of Joseph and Aseneth, the Acts of Silvester, and the legend of the Sleepers of Ephesus. Books 3–6 are an abridged Syriac version of the lost Greek Ecclesiastical History of Zechariah Rhetor, which covered the years 450–491; these books led to the attribution of the whole compilation to him. Books 7–12 cover the reigns of Anastasius, Justin I, Justinian, and Justin II down to 569. The chronicle is an important source for the christological controversies of the late 5th and 6th centuries.
